subject: Decision: SDN egress gateway approach for Private VPC on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Alex Kit <alex.kit@stellarbank.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: network-team@stellarbank.com
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: STELLAR: On-prem VPC egress model and control plane reachability

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. As we scope the on-prem Private deployment, our security team wants a clear recommendation for egress: they prefer an SDN-style egress gateway that sits in the customer network and terminates outbound traffic, but they also want confirmation on how the Redwood control plane will securely reach the data plane without opening broad inbound holes.

Two asks from our side:
- A short decision note outlining pros/cons of (A) control-plane-initiated outbound tunnel (customer -> Redwood) vs (B) customer-initiated GRE/IPsec to a Redwood ingress for control-plane callbacks.
- A diagram we can present to security showing the minimal ports required and where audit/logs are collected.

Can your team produce a short writeup and a reference diagram this week? We have a security sync on Mon 2026-10-05.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Kit
Senior Infra Architect, StellarBank

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Tagging internal folks to draft the note and diagram. Quick summary of proposed next steps from our side: 

1) We’ll prepare a 1-page decision memo comparing two viable patterns:
   - Option A: Customer-hosted SDN egress gateway + outbound-only control-plane tunnels (preferred for our managed control plane model).
   - Option B: Customer IPSec/GRE to Redwood ingress with mutual TLS and selective ports (preferred where customer policy forbids persistent outbound tunnels).

2) Produce a minimal ports diagram + audit/log placement (we’ll reference our standard: control-plane calls over mTLS on 443, metrics/health over 8443 optional).

3) Share attachments: sdn-proposal-v2.pdf and network-diagram-v3.png (first cut).

Irene, Laura, Hiro — can you review the attached draft and call out any operational caveats (KV cache, NAT, MTU) by EOD tomorrow?

Cheers,

Subject: Re: STELLAR: On-prem VPC egress model and control plane reachability

Quick notes after reading the draft:

- Option A (outbound control-plane tunnel):
  Pros: no inbound holes required, easier for customers with strict inbound ACLs. Keep sessions alive with periodic keepalives; negotiate MTU to avoid fragmentation across GRE.
  Cons: adds a stateful connection to maintain per-site; need to surface metrics for tunnel health into Redwood Console.

- Option B (customer-to-redwood IPSec/GRE to ingress):
  Pros: simpler topology diagram for security teams, central egress control at Redwood ingress.
  Cons: more exposed surface on Redwood side, requires us to run per-tenant ingress endpoints (impacts scaling) and tighter RBAC for callback endpoints.

Operational caveats I want called out in the memo:
- KV cache affinity: if we terminate tunnels on different pods, cold-cache penalties for long-running sessions. Recommend sticky routing for traffic that leverages large KV caches.
- NAT and port preservation: some customers do double-NAT; we must ensure health checks survive.
- Logging placement: prefer writing all access logs to S3-compatible endpoint owned by the customer + sending redwood-trace-id to our control plane so we can correlate.

I’ve added comments in the attached PDF (sdn-proposal-v2.pdf).

—Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: STELLAR: On-prem VPC egress model and control plane reachability

Thanks — picking up from Irene’s ops lens. A few implementation details we should surface in the decision note for Stellar security: 

- Health & failover: recommend two redundant outbound tunnels from customer SDN to Redwood (active/backup) with BFD for detection. Document expected failover times (<= 5s typical with BFD tuned).
- TLS mutual auth: we will require mTLS for control-plane/wire calls; cert rotation policy must be documented (30-day rotation for short-lived certs or 1 year for managed KMS).
- Audit retention: customer can opt to forward control-plane audit logs to their SIEM; default we keep 90 days in our system for enterprise customers.
- Egress policy enforcement: if Stellar wants egress filtering at their gateway, we recommend that as the canonical enforcement point (Redwood will not attempt to override).

I’ve updated network-diagram-v3.png with a callout for BFD and sticky routing.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Private Deployments

Date: 2026-10-04T15:43:00Z
Subject: Decision: SDN egress gateway + outbound-only control-plane tunnels (recommended)

Alex / Stellar team — thanks for the review cycle. Based on constraints you described and our operational analysis, Redwood recommends Option A: Customer-hosted SDN egress gateway with outbound-only control-plane tunnels to Redwood-managed control-plane endpoints. Summary and next steps below.

Decision rationale (short):
- Security: outbound-only model avoids exposing inbound ports in Stellar’s environment (aligns with your security policy).
- Operational: we support sticky routing and sticky KV affinity to avoid cold-cache regressions; BFD + dual-tunnel recommended for failover.
- Scaling: by keeping control-plane connections outbound, Redwood avoids per-tenant ingress scaling and central attack surface.

Minimal ports & requirements (for slide to security):
- Outbound mTLS from customer gateway to our control-plane endpoints on 443 (TCP).
- Optional metrics/health to 8443.
- Allow ICMP/BFD as negotiated for fast failover (optional, firewall-dependent).

Artifacts attached: sdn-proposal-v2.pdf (finalized with comments), network-diagram-v3.png (annotated). We also put a readout in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SDN+Egress+Gateway+Options

Next steps:
- Jonas/Laura: prepare a 1-slide security summary for 2026-10-05 security sync.
- Irene/Hiro: prepare runbook steps for tunnel provisioning and cert rotation (target 2026-10-09).
- Alex: confirm any additional SIEM endpoints or retention policy requirements.

If that all sounds good, we’ll send a short implementation checklist and a minimal Terraform snippet for Tunnel creation.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Jonas Weber
Staff Solutions Architect — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
